searchText: RLP encode/decode is probably the only remaining low hanging optimization fruit. The only hard part of this is exporting the data out of the clients (we probably need a custom RPC endpoint?). Importing it is really easy. I would look into whether `eth_getProof` gets you what you need: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1186 I can get you access to an archive node, but you can validate the idea by trying to execute blocks near the tip of the chain on a regular client that is fully synced. Actually `debug_accountRange` and `debug_storageRangeAt` exist, so we can use those. I have an Erigon archive node. I have no access at all to a geth node, so I have to rely on other people to catch geth specific bugs like the hex number format one you fixed. I assume that you guys would like me to open these as bugs in the `executions-specs` repository? ``` INFO:ethereum_spec_tools.sync:block 1149999 applied (took 0.00902197090908885s) Traceback (most recent call last): File "/home/pipermerriam/.virtualenvs/pyspec/bin/ethereum-spec-sync", line 33, in <module> sys.exit(load_entry_point('ethereum', 'console_scripts', 'ethereum-spec-sync')()) File "/home/pipermerriam/projects/execution-specs/src/ethereum_spec_tools/sync.py", line 572, in main sync.process_blocks() File "/home/pipermerriam/projects/execution-specs/src/ethereum_spec_tools/sync.py", line 548, in process_blocks self.module("spec").state_transition(self.chain, block) File "/home/pipermerriam/projects/execution-specs/src/ethereum/frontier/spec.py", line 174, in state_transition validate_header(block.header, parent_header) File "/home/pipermerriam/projects/execution-specs/src/ethereum/frontier/spec.py", line 221, in validate_header ensure(header.difficulty == block_difficulty) File "/home/pipermerriam/projects/execution-specs/src/ethereum/utils/ensure.py", line 42, in ensure raise exception_class() ethereum.utils.ensure.EnsureError ``` Is that the fork block? I remember it's somewhere around 1.1 million blocks. looks a lot like a fork block to me I don't think we've put up the homestead fork yet well, looks like I successfully synced all of Frontier!? Rather I know we haven't put it in `ethereum/execution-specs` but if you're running voith's branch then it's a bug. Looks like! Here is pypy profile of a sync of all of frontier: https://pastebin.com/tSVdjv8J. Rough breakdown is: 33% calculating state roots 28% processing transactions 19% checking POWs 11% persisting stuff to disk (this is on HDD) I _still_ haven't been able to sync frontier after a couple days I have persist disabled But you and Piper have done it. Bloody weird. My laptop isn't _that_ bad. Under 10% memory used, the rest of my machine is totally usable. I don't think it's trashing or anything 🤪 how does the project maintain parity between the optimized and non-optimized implementations? I don't think we are running the test suite with both the optimized and non-optimized implementations. I think we should create separate jobs on CI for this. Assuming the APIs are the same, this may also be a good place for hypothesis/fuzz-testing/property-based-testing
